question: _________ is considered as the holy person who gave Jainism its present form.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahavira.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahavira,** also known as Vardhamana, was the **24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism.**
 
• He is credited with formulating the core principles and teachings of Jainism as we know them today.
 
• Mahavira is credited with adding the **fifth vow, Brahmacharya (Chastity)**, to the existing four vows, making up the **Panchamahavrat **(Five Great Vows) in Jainism. 
 
• Mahavira’s teachings emphasize non-violence (Ahimsa), truth (Satya), non-stealing (Asteya), chastity (Brahmacharya), and non-possession (Aparigraha).
 
• He attained enlightenment through intense meditation and asceticism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Rishabhanatha is believed to be the** first Tirthankara of Jainism **and is also known as Adinatha.
 
• Vasudev and Digambar are not directly related to the reformulation of Jainism; Vasudev is often associated with Hindu mythology, and Digambara is one of the two main sects of Jainism, the other being Svetambara.
 
• The teachings of Mahavira and the philosophy of Jainism are detailed in texts like the** Agamas and Kalpasutra.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__****Digambara (Sky-Clad)**

 
• Monks do not wear any clothes, symbolizing renunciation of worldly possessions.
 
• Believe that women must be reborn as men to achieve liberation.
 
• Recognize texts like the **Samayasara and Pravachanasara.**
 
• **Sub-sects:**
 
• Bisapantha
 
• Terapantha
 
• Taranapantha
 
• Gumanapantha

**Svetambara (White-Clad)**

 
• Monks and nuns wear white clothes.
 
• Believe that women can achieve liberation.
 
• Recognize texts like the **Agamas and Kalpa Sutra.**
 
• **Sub-sects:**
 
• Murtipujaka (Idol Worshippers)
 
• Sthanakvasi (Non-Idol Worshippers)
 
• Terapanthi (Reformist group within Sthanakvasi)
